written:
2026-10-29, before any matter-floor value in a dynamical gauge ensemble had been computed. Known at this time: the Phase V-C Wilson theory (engine G) on the FR30 level-4 patch (inter-tile

= 0.103 -> 0.566 for beta = 0.4 -> 1.6, crossover between beta = 1.6 and 2.0); the frozen-background floors of the pinned supertile T3: 1387 Y3 = 9.95592, 539311 Y3 = 9.95733, FR30 Y3 = 9.37847, 937 Y3 = 8.49106; the trivial connection on T3: 1.66951 (Phase XIII label-extended trivial block).
question: When the Q8 gauge field on the chair hull is dynamical (Wilson action), does the Chair44 matter floor survive as an order parameter, and are the frame-rule backgrounds typical or atypical configurations of the ensemble?

model.complex: phase5c_q8_gauge.fr30_complex(3): dual cubical complex of the pinned level-3 chair supertile (512 tiles, 3584 unit cubes); dual links = unit faces between cubes; links inside a tile frozen to 1 (rigid tiles); plaquettes = 2x2 squares of cubes
model.action: S[U] = beta * sum_p (1 - (1/2) Re Tr U_p), U_l in Q8, all plaquettes of the complex (intra-tile links contribute 1)
model.sampler: phase5c_q8_gauge.General (exact heat bath over the 8 elements, greedy colouring), unchanged
model.matter: H_U = 24 - sum over dynamical links l = (x, mu) of [L(U_l) at (own x, own x+mu) + L(U_l)^T at (own x+mu, own x)], L(q) the 4x4 real left multiplication by the quaternion q (the realified spinor form of Phases X-XIII, eigenvalues doubled); pinned: diagonal 24 on every tile. lambda_min(H_U) by dense eigvalsh
model.gauge covariance: tile-wise gauge transformations g_a act as U_l -> g_(own x) U_l g_(own x+mu)^-1 and preserve both the action and spec(H_U)

run.starts: for each beta independently: hot (uniform random links) and cold (all 1); seeds 0 (hot) and 1 (cold)
run.measurements:
40 configurations per beta and start, 10 sweeps apart; observables per configuration: inter-tile

, -1 plaquette density, lambda_min(H_U)
run.errors: standard error over the 40 configurations (they are 10 sweeps apart); reported per start; hot and cold reported separately and averaged only where they agree within 3 standard errors

checks_before_predictions_are_scored: C1: at beta = infinity (cold start, no sweeps) lambda_min(H_1) equals the trivial-connection floor of T3, 1.66951 (to 1e-6): the complex and the matter operator match the Phase XII-XIII geometry
C2: gauge covariance: lambda_min is unchanged (to 1e-9) under 3 random tile-wise gauge transformations of one sampled configuration
C3: at beta = 0 the sampled links are uniform (each of the 8 elements within 5 percent of 1/8 over all dynamical links of the 40 configurations)

predictions.H1 (monotone order parameter): <lambda_min>(beta) is non-increasing in beta: no increase between consecutive betas larger than 3 standard errors (hot-start series)
predictions.H2 (the frontier backgrounds are atypica: at every beta, Y3(1387) = 9.95592 exceeds the largest lambda_min among all 80 sampled configurations (hot and cold)
predictions.H3 (the floor tracks deconfinement):
the beta at which falls fastest (largest drop between consecutive grid points, hot start) is within one grid step of the beta at which inter-tile

rises fastest

failure: each of H1, H2, H3 is scored separately as holds / fails; a failure is reported as [F] with the data; nothing is refitted
labels: [E] floating-point evidence from a simulated (Monte Carlo) ensemble on one finite patch; no continuum, infinite-volume or physical claim follows from it
meaning: a first dynamical test of whether the Chair44 frustration floor is a property of a typical gauge field or of the specific frame-rule backgrounds
